initial_prompt:
Review this scoped FileBackup draft correction for concrete HIGH-RISK failure cases only. Confirm all seven attachment END markers, 40 new Drafted LLRs and 41 planned cases; 12 accepted SRs and assumptions are context. No tools or source access, no test execution. Existing system: content addressed pool in CurrentBackup shards and flat BackupHistory dated folders, prior state saved before latest per-file checkpoints, superseded moves last, no backup deletion of objects, carried PS/bash recovery independent of engine. Do not infer unshown runtime implementation.

Owner decision: last-known valid checkpoint definitions are recoverable even if the latest scan was interrupted. Remove blanket INCOMPLETE_RUN classification. Copy pre-run MANIFEST.csv and DIRECTORIES.csv to .prev before latest mutations, never overwrite existing copies on later runs, delete them only after successful backup. They preserve definitions, not extra content or new retention guarantee. Current defaults remain usable; explicit previous selection never mixes old/current records. A partial previous set is reported, not rebuilt from newer data. Initial copy failure stops before latest changes; existing partial residue is kept until successful completion. Existing snapshots provide normal prior-state history. Source scan completion is different from recovery of recorded information. This is intentional, not a finding to strengthen into whole-tree transactional capture or arbitrary external deletion defense.

Folders/links enter semantic change detection. In-root folder links are relative on restore, supported destination inside restored root; external folder links restore expanded ordinary duplicate outputs, deduplicated in stored pool; file links are captured ordinary bytes. Current mandatory-metadata revision writes header-only empty sidecar; concrete admission is N1 design work. Retention remains accepted cutoff latest/later protection. Independent external writers or manual deletion bypass protocol.

Only raise concrete credible loss of protected data, incorrect claimed recovery, serious containment failure, or contradictory required outcomes. Missing implementation/normal design work/performance measurements are not new high-risk findings by themselves. Do not repeat prior marker review as authority. At most three findings, no quota, under 700 words. Give exact clause/causal sequence and smallest correction within owner's choices. If no qualifying issue, say so. Treat partial-copy creation/deletion honestly; do not assume an unstated overwrite, automatic fallback or destructive whole-pool sweep. State limits and do not list lower-risk suggestions.
followup_prompt:
Re-evaluate the two high-risk findings, within the owner's scope. First confirm the SEVEN actual attachments by basename: accepted-sr-context.json, assumptions.toml, contracts.md, draft-cases.toml, draft-llrs.toml, flows.md, owner-prev-review.md. Your report listed seven names but called them six and introduced unattached review.md; clarify whether this was a count typo. Do not claim unobserved inputs.

Finding 1: LLR164 already required preserving independently recoverable file bytes when supplemental metadata conflicts. LLR174's broader conflict wording could obscure that. The sole normative clarification now is: validate/reject unsafe or colliding FILE rows as before, but reject only the supplemental DIRECTORY/LINK record when it conflicts with independently valid manifest file paths. Restore valid files through safe ordinary parents; report metadata damage. Existing unsafe target redirects still refuse affected writes. This rule depends on record roles, never timestamps or .prev presence. TC284 now tests this. No pairing transaction, marker or requirement that all source entries were already recorded is added. Does this close the concrete conflict scenario without strengthening checkpoint scope?

Finding 2 is rejected pending a supported causal scenario. LLR163 says: 'Move superseded objects only after final latest publication and only when no final latest row depends on them; the destination is a state that records the identity. A failed move leaves the available copy intact and reports failure.' It does NOT restrict relocation to files captured in this invocation. Existing algorithm scans final latest dependencies and moves interrupted-run leftovers to the history state naming them. Even if a move is delayed, the object remains available in CurrentBackup's valid shard and is discoverable by the shared pool: being unreferenced by the latest manifest is not being misplaced or deleted. The loop never deletes objects. 'Remove unneeded NEW snapshot' does not delete an older saved prior state. Finally, your 'if killed before date1 rename' alternative cannot coexist with the subsequent checkpoint: prior snapshot publication is BEFORE any latest checkpoint. Do not invent a prune that ignores its protected dependency/rehoming checks. .prev intentionally stays auxiliary; making it the automatic change baseline would violate owner intent and is not justified by this scenario. Reassess high-risk status and withdraw if unsupported.

Return final disposition, any actual remaining HIGH-RISK causal issue only, and limits. No quota, no lower-risk additions. The correction to LLR174/TC284 above is the complete changed scope since your input; approved SRs and all other supplied semantics are unchanged.
